summary:
Team Smart Star developed 90 Sols to Forever: The Twin Explorers of Mars, a 10-page illustrated digital comic designed for school-age space enthusiasts. Utilizing Synthetic Intelligence (SI) tools alongside human-verified NASA mission logs, the comic chronicles the historic journeys of the Spirit and Opportunity Mars rovers from their 2003 launch to their final transmissions in 2010 and 2019.

The project directly addresses the challenge by transforming complex planetary engineering into an emotionally resonant, story-driven narrative rather than a dry list of facts. By illustrating real operational milestones—such as using the Rock Abrasion Tool to discover hematite "blueberries," dragging a broken wheel to uncover pure silica, and escaping sand traps via Earth-based simulations—the comic connects each rover's hardware directly to the scientific breakthroughs they made possible.

This work is important because it inspires young learners to build a personal connection with the robotic pioneers resting silently on Mars. Showing how machines built for 90 days survived for years teaches students resilience, creative problem-solving, and how past discoveries paved the way for modern Martian exploration.
details:
90 Sols to Forever: The Twin Explorers of Mars is a 10-page illustrated digital comic created by Team Smart Star to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the engineering and scientific legacy of NASA’s twin Mars Exploration Rovers, Spirit and Opportunity (2004–2019). Readers follow a sequential visual narrative from the rovers' 2003 launch in Cape Canaveral to their final resting places in Gusev Crater and Perseverance Valley. Each page pairs authentic historical mission milestones with clear, accessible explanations of how specific hardware—such as the Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT), six-wheeled rocker-bogie suspension, and solar arrays—enabled groundbreaking planetary science.

Instead of presenting space hardware as a dry list of technical specifications, this comic builds an emotional and intellectual bridge between young readers and the robotic explorers resting silently on Mars. By framing Spirit and Opportunity as resilient pioneers that outlived their original 90-sol mission by years, the project aims to spark curiosity in STEM, planetary geology, and space engineering among upper-elementary and middle-school students. Showing how engineering failures (like Spirit’s jammed front wheel) and environmental hazards (like Opportunity’s sand traps) were overcome through human ingenuity on Earth demonstrates how past discoveries paved the way for modern rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance.

To keep the storytelling engaging without relying on cartoonish tropes, Team Smart Star adopted a grounded, graphic-novel aesthetic using warm Martian palettes and cross-hatched technical line art. We used relatable visual metaphors—such as calling hematite spherules "blueberries" and framing Opportunity’s 42.195 km journey as an extraterrestrial marathon—while maintaining strict scientific and historical accuracy throughout.

In developing this project, our team utilized historical NASA Mars Exploration Rover (MER) mission logs, planetary geology archives, collaborative scriptwriting tools, and Synthetic Intelligence (SI) assistance for drafting narrative dialogue and rendering sequential comic illustrations. Throughout development, we prioritized audience accessibility, verified every discovery (such as hematite, pure silica from ancient hot springs, and neutral-pH gypsum veins) against real mission data, and strictly followed NASA Space Apps SI usage guidelines by documenting our SI workflow, excluding restricted agency logos, and retaining visible watermarks on all generated visuals.
